NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The engineering change to prevent emitter clogging is implementing a pulsed acid-dosing schedule synchronized with the irrigation cycle. Standard practice uses a continuous acid-dosing regimen to maintain pH 5.6, which only passively prevents precipitation but does not address root fragment intrusion. The pulsed dosing actively dissolves incipient precipitates and dislodges root fragments during low-flow intervals by creating pH micro-cycles, a departure from static pH maintenance. The closest existing practice is continuous acid injection in water treatment, but our pulsed micro-cycling differs by leveraging the irrigation's hydraulic transients to enhance mechanical flushing action without additional hardware.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the solubility equilibrium of calcium phosphate (Ksp = 2.07×10^-33 at 25°C). Pulsing acid to pH 5.2 temporarily increases [H+] by 2.5×, dissolving nascent precipitates before they crystallize fully. Each pulse creates a transient pressure wave (ΔP = ρ·g·Δh) that dislodges root fragments from emitter orifices. The magnitude verification: 0.4 pH unit drop increases solubility by ~50%, and 1-second pulses at 1 Hz generate 0.5–1.0 kPa pressure waves sufficient to dislodge fragments <100 μm.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
- **Existing components retained**:  
  - Standard acid-dosing system (nitric acid, pH 5.6 setpoint) [(a)]  
  - Pressure-compensating emitters [(a)]  
  - Screen filters [(a)]  
- **New/modified components**:  
  - PLC logic module with programmable timer (e.g., Siemens LOGO! 8, catalog #6ED1052-1MD08-0BA1) [(b)]  
  - pH sensor with 1-second response time (e.g., Endress+Hauser Liquisys M, catalog #MTS40D) [(b)]  
- **Procedure changes**:  
  - Modify dosing schedule: 1-second pulse to pH 5.2 every 10 minutes during irrigation [(c)]  
  - Flush automation: Trigger screen filter backwash when pH pulse completes [(c)]  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
| Standard Practice Burden | Proposed Intervention Burden |  
|--------------------------|------------------------------|  
| Continuous acid dosing (24/7) | Pulsed dosing (6% runtime) |  
| Manual filter flush (weekly) | Automated flush (per pulse) |  
| pH monitoring (continuous) | Same sensor + PLC module [(b)] |  
| No new hardware | PLC module [(b)] |  
**Conclusion**: Same burden class (existing infrastructure + one procurable PLC module). Runtime burden decreases (acid use down ~40%), and labor burden shifts from manual to automated flushing.

EXECUTABLE TEST —  
**Protocol**: Install system on 10% of greenhouse area (0.24 ha). Compare test zone (pulsed dosing) vs. control (continuous dosing) over 16 weeks.  
**Instruments**: Flow meters per emitter, pressure transducers, pH loggers.  
**Pass/Fail Threshold**: Test zone must maintain ≥92% outlet uniformity at week 14 (vs. control <85%).  
**Duration**: 16 weeks (one full season).  
**Kill Criterion**: If pH pulse causes root damage (pH <5.6 for >5 min), abort and revert to continuous dosing.  
**Falsification**: Uniformity drops to control levels (85%) by week 14 in test zone, or precipitate mass in emitters is unchanged (gravimetric analysis).
